spans.s:
वम् वम्, cl. 1. P. वमति (Ved. also
वमिति), ववाम (2nd sing. ववमिथ,
3rd pl. ववमुस् by Pāṇ.

; according to
some वेमिथ, वेमुस्), वमिष्यति, अवमीत् (Pāṇ.
VII. 2, 5

), वमितुम्, to vomit, eject from the
mouth, spit out; to eject, emit, send forth, give
forth, give out, give off, divulge; to reject: Pass.
वम्यते, Aor. अवामि (Part. वान्त and वमित):
Caus. वामयति, वमयति (with prepositions the
latter only is used), -यितुम्, Aor. अवीवमत्, to cause
to vomit, sicken: Desid. विवमिषति: Intens. वं-
वम्यते, वंवन्ति; [cf. Zend vam, ‘to vomit;’
Gr. ἐμ-έ-ω, ἔμ-ε-το-ς, ἔμ-εσι-ς; Lat. vom-o, vom-
i-tu-s, vom-i-tio; Goth. vamm, ana-vammjan;
Angl. Sax. wemman; Old Norse vom-a, vœma;
Lith. vem-j-u, vem-ti, vem-alai.]
वम, अस्, ई, m. f. vomiting, ejecting, giving out.

1. वाम, अस्, m. (for 2. see below), the act of
vomiting.

वाम 2. वाम, अस्, आ or ई, अम् (according to
Uṇādi-s. 1. 139. fr. rt. 2. वा; according to others
fr. rt. 1. वन्, ‘to hurt or to like’), reverse, adverse,
opposite, contrary, inverted; left, not right; crooked;
bad, vile, base, wicked; short; beautiful, handsome,
pleasing; (अस्), m., N. of Śiva; of Kāma (god of
love); a breast, udder; a pot-herb, Chenopodium
Album; an animal, sentient being; a snake; (अम्),
n. anything desirable or pleasing, wealth, possessions;
(आ), f. a woman; N. of Gaurī; of Lakṣmī; of
Sarasvatī; (ई), f. a mare; a she-ass; a young
female elephant; the female of the jackal; [cf. Old
Germ. winistar; Angl. Sax. wynstre.]
—वाम-
जात, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. produced from wealth.
—वा-
म-जुष्ट, अम्, n., N. of a Tantra work (= वाम-
केश्वर-तन्त्र).
—वाम-ता, f. or वाम-त्व, अम्,
n. contrariety, perverseness; wickedness, craftiness;
[]
disfavour; loveliness.
—वाम-दृश्, क्, f. a woman.
—वाम-देव, अस्, m., N. of a Vedic Ṛṣi (having
the patronymic Gautama, author of the hymns Ṛg-
veda
IV. 1

— 41, 45 — 48, comprising nearly the whole
fourth Maṇḍala); of Śiva; of an author.
—वाम-
देव्य, अस्, m. a patronymic of Aṃho-muc (author
of Ṛg-veda

); of Bṛhad-uktha; of Mūrdhan-
vat.
—वाम-नीति, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. leading or guiding
to wealth, (Sāy. on Ṛg-veda

. वननीया-
नां धनानां नेतृ.)
—वाम-नेत्र, अम्, n. a
mystical name of the long vowel ई; (आ), f. a woman
with beautiful eyes, a handsome woman in general.
—वाम-मार्ग, अस्, m. the left hand way or ritual;
see वामाचार.
—वाम-लोचन, अस्, आ, अम्, fine-
eyed; (आ), f. a handsome-eyed woman.
—वाम-
शील, अस्, आ, अम्, refractory in disposition; (अस्), m.
an epithet of Kāma.
—वामाक्ष (˚म-अक्˚), अस्, ई,
अम्, having beautiful eyes; (ई), f. a woman with
lovely eyes.
—वामाक्षि (˚म-अक्˚), इ, n. the left eye.
—वामाचार (˚म-आच्˚), अस्, m. the left hand ritual
or doctrine of the Tantras, i. e. the worship of the
Śakti or Female Energy personified as the wife of
Śiva according to the grosser system (in which the
eating of flesh, drinking of spirits, &c. is practised,
cf. दक्षिणाचार).
—वामाचारिन्, ई, m. a follower
of the left hand ritual of the Tantras.
—वामापीडन
(˚म-आप्˚?), अस्, m. the tree Salvadora Persica, &c.
(= पीलु).
—वामावर्त (˚म-आव्˚), अस्, m. a conch-
shell with the spiral running from right to left.
—वामोरु (˚म-ऊरु˚), उस्, उस् or ऊस्, उ, having
handsome thighs; (उस् or ऊस्), f. a handsome-thighed
woman.
—वामोरु-तरा or वामोरू-तरा, f. a very
handsome-thighed woman.

वमथु, उस्, m. vomiting, ejecting from the
mouth; water ejected from an elephant's trunk; =
काश, a cough (?) .

वमन, अम्, n. the act of vomiting, ejecting
anything from the mouth; causing vomiting, an
emetic; offering oblations to fire; taking, getting;
pain, paining; (अस्), m. hemp; (आस्), m. pl., N. of
a people; (ई), f. a leech.

वामन वामन, अस्, आ, अम् (probably fr. 2. वा-
म; said to be fr. rt. वम्), dwarfish, short in stature,
a dwarf; depressed, pressed flat or down; low, vile,
base; (अस्), m. Viṣṇu in his dwarf incarnation, (this
was the fifth of the descents of Viṣṇu, and under-
taken to humble the pride of the Daitya Bali, who
had acquired dominion over the three worlds [see
बलि]; the germ of the story of this incarnation
seems to be contained in Śatapatha-Br.

,
the later legend is given in Rāmāyaṇa

);
the elephant that supports the south quarter; the tree
Alangium Hexapetalum; N. of the author of the
Kāvyālaṅkāra-vṛtti; of the Kāśikā-vṛtti commen-
tary; (आ), f., N. of an Apsaras; (ई), f. a female
dwarf; a sort of woman; a mare; a disease of the
Vagina.
—वामन-तनु, उस्, उस् or वी, उ, dwarf-
bodied.
—वामन-पुराण, अम्, n., N. of one
of the eighteen Purāṇas (said to have been related
by Pulastya to Nārada, and containing an account
of the dwarf incarnation of Viṣṇu; see पुराण).
—वामन-प्रादुर्भाव, अस्, m. the manifestation
or incarnation of the dwarf; see above.
—वामन-
रूपिन्, ई, इणी, इ, dwarf-formed, being in the form of
a dwarf.
—वामन-वृत्ति, इस्, f., N. of a commen-
tary on Pāṇini's grammar by Vāmana Jayāditya, (see
काशिक.)
—वामन-वृत्ति-टीका, f., N. of a commen-
tary by Maheśvara on the Kāvyālaṅkāra-vṛtti.
—वा-
मन-व्रत, अम्, n., N. of a particular Vrata to be
observed on the twelfth day of Śrāvaṇa in celebration
of Viṣṇu's dwarf incarnation.
—वामन-सूक्त, अम्,
n., N. of a Vedic hymn.
—वामन-स्वामिन्, ई, m.,
N. of a poet.
—वामनाकृति (˚न-आक्˚), इस्, इस्, इ,
dwarf-shaped, dwarfish.
—वामनाचार्य (˚न-आच्˚),
अस्, m., N. of a commentator.
—वामनावतार (˚न-
अव्˚), अस्, m. the dwarf incarnation; see under वामन
above.
—वामनावतार-कथन, अम्, n. the story
of the dwarf incarnation, N. of a chapter of the
Padma-Purāṇa.
—वामनी-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, pressed
down, shortened, flattened.
—वामनेन्द्र-स्वा-
मिन्, ई, m. a proper N.
—वामनोपपुराण (˚न-
उप्˚), अम्, n., N. of an Upa-Purāṇa.
वमनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be vomited; (आ), f. a fly.

वमि, इस्, f. vomiting, sickness, nausea, qualmishness;
an emetic; (इस्), m., N. of fire; a rogue, cheat.

वमित, अस्, आ, अम्, vomited, made to vomit,
sickened.

वमितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be vomited, to be
ejected from the mouth.
वमित्वा, ind. having vomited, having been sick.
वमिन्, ई, इनी, इ, vomiting, being sick.

वामिन्, ई, इनी, इ, vomiting, ejecting from the
mouth.
वम्भ वम्भ, अस्, m. = वंश, a bamboo, &c.

वम्भारव वम्भा-रव, अस्, m. (onomato-
poetic), the lowing of cattle, (better written बम्भा-
रव.)

वम्मागदेश वम्माग-देश, अस्, m., N. of a
district.

वम्र वम्र, अस्, m. (or more frequently)
ई, f. (probably connected with वल्मी), an ant, (said
to be also आ, f.); (अस्), m. a proper N., (Vamra
Vaikhānasa is the author of the hymn Ṛg-veda

); [cf. Gr. μύρμο-ς, μύρμ-ηξ; Lat. form-ica.]
—वम्री-कूट, अम्, n. an ant-hill.

वम्रक, अस्, m., Ved. a small ant; (अस्, आ, अम्),
small, little (= ह्रस्व, according to Naigh.
III. 2

1. वामक, अस्, &c. (for 2. see col. 3), one who
vomits.

2. वामक, अस्, आ, अम्, left, not right; (अम्), n.
a kind of gesture.
—वामकेश्वर-तन्त्र (˚क-ईश्˚),
अम्, n., N. of a Tantra work.
वामिका, f. an epithet of the goddess Durgā.
वामनिका, f. a female dwarf; a sort of woman.

वामलूर वामलूर, अस्, m. (connected with
[]
वम्रा, वल्मी, वल्मीक), an ant-hill, mole-hill,
hillock thrown up by white ants.

वामनक, अस्, आ, अम्, = वामन, dwarfish, a
dwarf; (अस्), m. epithet of a man born under a par-
ticular constellation; N. of a mountain; (इका), f.,
N. of one of the Mātṛs attending on Skanda; (अम्),
n. the form of a dwarf; N. of a place of pilgrimage
(called after Viṣṇu in his dwarf-incarnation).
